The mediastinum is midline and has a normal width, and the hilar regions do not show any significant lymphadenopathy or masses. The pleural spaces are also clear; the costophrenic angles on both the left and right sides are sharp, confirming the absence of pleural effusion. No air is seen in the pleural space, which would suggest a pneumothorax.

There are no cortical discontinuities or displacements to suggest an acute fracture. The diaphragm is well-defined and has a normal dome-shaped contour on both sides, with the right side being slightly higher than the left, which is a normal physiological finding. No signs of discoid or plate-like densities are visible to suggest atelectasis.
